title: Be honest… you already know the answer before you even finish asking the question.
paragraphs: Be honest… you already know the answer before you even finish asking the question.

You open your Bible.
You say a prayer.
You check the box.
But your mind is somewhere else.
You’re thinking about messages, deadlines, problems, people… everything except the God you’re supposedly meeting.
And deep down, there’s that quiet thought you try to ignore:
“This doesn’t feel real.”

You don’t say it out loud.
But you feel it.
You finish your “time with God” and walk away unchanged.

Same worries.
Same habits.
Same sins you promised last night you’d stop.
And you tell yourself, “At least I tried.”
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
God was never after your routine.
He was after you.

Not your schedule.
Not your streak.
Not your religious consistency.
You.
“‘These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.’” — Matthew 15:8
Read that again.
You can say the right words and still be far from Him.
You can read chapters and still not hear His voice.
You can pray daily and still not know Him.
That’s the tension you’ve been feeling.
Because something in you knows… this isn’t what it’s supposed to be.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
Think about it.
When was the last time you sat with God and didn’t rush?
When was the last time His Word cut you… exposed you… stopped you mid-verse because it hit too close?
“When the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword… discerning the thoughts and intentions of the heart.” — Hebrews 4:12

If your time with God never confronts you,
never interrupts you,
never convicts you…
then you’re not encountering Him.
You’re managing Him.
And that’s dangerous.
Because routine without relationship creates the illusion of faith.
You start believing you’re close to God simply because you spend time near spiritual things.
But proximity isn’t intimacy.

Judas walked with Jesus.
He heard every sermon.
Saw every miracle.
And still betrayed Him.
God saw it.
You knew.
So what’s really happening?

You’re showing up physically…
but withholding yourself spiritually.

You read, but don’t surrender.
You pray, but don’t listen.
You sit, but don’t engage.
Because real time with God is costly.

It will expose your pride.
It will confront your sin.
It will call you to change.
And that’s where most people pull back.
Because routine is safe.
Real relationship isn’t.
“Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you.” — James 4:8
But look at what comes next:
“Cleanse your hands… purify your hearts… be wretched and mourn and weep…”
That’s not comfortable.
That’s not casual.
That’s real.
And real is what you’ve been avoiding.

Not intentionally.
But consistently.
You’ve settled for moments instead of surrender.
But there’s another side to this.
Because when your time with God becomes real…
everything changes.

You stop performing.
You start encountering.

Scripture stops being words on a page
and becomes a mirror you can’t look away from.

Prayer stops being repetition
and becomes conversation that breaks you and rebuilds you.
And slowly…
your desires shift.
Your sensitivity to sin increases.
Your hunger for Him grows.
“Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.” — Psalm 51:10
That prayer doesn’t come from routine.
It comes from desperation.
And maybe that’s what’s been missing.
Not discipline.
Desperation.
Because people who know they need God don’t rush Him.
They cling to Him.
So now you’re at a quiet crossroads.
You can keep going the way you’ve been going…

keep doing your routine,
keep calling it “time with God,”
keep walking away unchanged.
Or you can be honest.
You can admit that something’s off.

You can come to Him not polished,
not perfect,
not pretending…
but real.
Broken if you have to be.
Because that’s where grace meets you.
“God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.” — James 4:6

Not the routine.
Not the performance.
The humble.
So if something in you is stirring right now…

That conviction you feel?
That discomfort?
That’s not guilt trying to trap you.
That’s God trying to wake you up.
Say it plainly if it’s true:
“My time with God hasn’t been real.”
There’s no freedom in pretending.
There’s freedom in truth.
And if you know someone who’s been stuck in routine like this… send this to them. Not to expose them—but to wake them up.
Stay close, because this is where deeper discipleship begins—not surface habits, but real transformation that confronts, corrects, and rebuilds your walk with Christ.
Follow this journey. Save this. Come back when you feel yourself drifting again.
